solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cover is more elegant without repetition

indicators.note: the doubled letter in the synonym loses its repeat, so one of the pair goes

parts.note: smoother means more polished or more elegant

explanation.surface: A remark that one thing looks more refined if nothing is repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without repetition' drops one O from SMOOTHER, the doubled letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover something thickly, as with a blanket or sauce, is a synonym sense of the verb.

clue.text: Piece of embroidery is small, getting bigger

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
ampler means larger or more plentiful

explanation.surface: A small piece of needlework that keeps growing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stitched panel showing a range of stitches or letters, a traditional piece of needlework.

clue.text: Disarray as roman type employed in galleys?

indicators.note: Disarray signals that the following letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Printing terms: roman type in a mess, as used in galley proofs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' and 'galleys' pretend to be printing words; a galley is also a rowed ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleys were ships powered by rowers, so a rower is a kind of person employed in one.

clue.text: Detect sound of clock keeping seconds down

parts.note: to hear is to detect the sound of something

indicators.note: keeping says the clock's sound holds the abbreviation within it

parts.note: the sound a clock makes is a tick

explanation.surface: Listening to a clock ticking as the seconds go down.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being low in spirits, and a sad heart is the same depressed mood.

clue.text: Sorrel or bay, main leaves seared on prepared food

indicators.note: leaves says the word for the main departs from seared

parts.note: the main is a literary name for the sea
a dish is prepared food

explanation.surface: Cookery: sorrel and bay leaves seared over a prepared dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Sorrel and bay look like herbs, but they are horse colours; 'leaves' is a verb, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrel and bay are horses' coat colours, both shades of brownish red.

clue.text: Notorious robber mostly got around injunction when trading was shaken up

indicators.note: got around says the first piece surrounds the second
mostly means the last letter of the robber's name is cut off

parts.note: Ronnie Biggs, one of the Great Train Robbers of 1963
a ban is a prohibiting order, an injunction

explanation.surface: A famous criminal evading a court order at a time of market upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Biggs was a British Great Train Robber who fled abroad; 'mostly' drops his final letter, and 'got around' wraps the rest round the ban.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1986 deregulation of the London Stock Exchange was nicknamed this, a sudden shake-up of trading.

clue.text: Blooming after all the rest in part of garden

indicators.note: in places the last-place word inside the garden bed

parts.note: a bed is a planted part of a garden
last means after all the others

explanation.surface: A flower blooming later than the others in a garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks floral but is a mild British curse word, like 'damned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild euphemistic intensifiers for 'damned', used to vent annoyance.

clue.text: Billions overlooked in gibberish which underlies peak in housing?

indicators.note: overlooked in says one letter is missed out from the nonsense word

parts.note: gabble is rapid unintelligible talk

explanation.surface: Billions ignored amid economic jargon about a housing price peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peak in housing' suggests a property boom; it is a roof's apex. GABBLE has two Bs and one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular end wall sits beneath the point of a pitched roof, holding up the ridge.

clue.text: Male ejected from wedding when one's raised high temper

indicators.note: is raised means the letter for one moves higher up in this down entry
ejected from says the male letter is thrown out of the wedding word

parts.note: a marriage is a wedding
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man thrown out of a wedding reception, tempers flaring.
explanation.walkthrough: Without M, MARRIAGE is ARRIAGE; in a down entry 'raised' moves the I up, earlier, to give AIRRAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury in flight, a temper at altitude, is the passenger's outburst on an aircraft.

clue.text: I must leave in a hurry after beginning to get very ill

indicators.note: after puts the hurry word behind the first letter
beginning to takes only the opening letter of the word get
must leave says the letter I goes from the word for hurriedly

parts.note: hastily means in a hurry

explanation.surface: Someone must dash off because they are starting to feel terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking dreadfully pale and sick is one sense, as in 'feeling ghastly' after a bad night.

clue.text: In Riviera's setting, one is right about fabulous girl

indicators.note: In puts the reversed piece inside the abbreviation for the sea

parts.note: the Riviera lies on the Mediterranean, the Med

indicators.note: about turns the words for one is and right backwards

parts.note: one is can be rendered I am

explanation.surface: Someone on the Riviera claims to be right about a wonderful young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns I AM R into RMAI, which sits 'In' MED.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous here means from fable: a sea maiden of legend is a mythical girl.

clue.text: Banff setting theatre blatantly uses in review

indicators.note: in review means looked back over, read in the opposite direction
uses means the answer is drawn from within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A drama critic notes that a theatre's production flagrantly borrows material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses' picks ATREBLA from theatre blatantly and 'in review' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff, the national park and town, lies in this Canadian province in the Rockies.

clue.text: Packing semi-automatic rifle, came to Land's End

indicators.note: Packing says the word for came to land holds the rifle inside it

parts.note: lit means alighted or came to land, as a bird does
the M1 Garand was the American semi-automatic rifle

explanation.surface: Someone armed with a rifle travels to the far tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England; the clue splits the name so 'End' alone is the definition. The rifle's M1 is entered with the digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or furthest point, which is what an end is.

clue.text: Unscramble hint before another turns up against it

indicators.note: Unscramble tells us to rearrange the letters of the following word
turns means the second word is read backwards

parts.note: another hint, i.e. a trace, a slight suggestion

explanation.surface: An instruction to decode a clue before another one appears against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another hint, a trace, which 'turns' backwards; 'Unscramble' gives INTH from hint.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British idiom for being in trouble, which is what being up against it means.

clue.text: Threaten to break banks, as secondary school administrator must do

definitions.meaning: a swollen river is close to bursting its banks

definitions.text: as secondary school administrator must do
definitions.meaning: a secondary school is a high school, which its head must manage

explanation.surface: A river close to flooding, compared with the duties of a head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: to run a high school.
explanation.definitionFit: A river swollen to the brim is said to be at this level; emotions can also be said to do it.

clue.text: Unstable prohibitionist harnesses extra energy

indicators.note: harnesses says the outer word holds the others within it

parts.note: a dry is someone who backs a ban on alcohol
odd means spare or extra, as in an odd sock
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A shaky temperance campaigner finds a surplus of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and tottering on one's feet, as the elderly may be, is what unstable describes.

clue.text: Lie marked out as unrealistic

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A falsehood flagged as fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with the quality of a vision in sleep is fanciful rather than true to life.

clue.text: Enjoy loose domesticity with drudge when in drink

indicators.note: in puts the drudge inside the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a hack is a drudge who does dull work for hire

explanation.surface: Settling into a casual home life with a menial worker over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To live together without marrying is the informal phrasal verb's sense, a loose domestic arrangement.

clue.text: Dash past with run for good place to get bronze?

indicators.note: Dash as a verb means to smash, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sprinter dashes past and runs for a medal place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bronze' suggests third place in a race; it is a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered sunny spot is where one acquires a tan, a bronzed skin.

clue.text: Pardon little woman for decorating home

indicators.note: decorating puts the woman's name around the home, like trimming

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: Asking forgiveness of a small woman for doing up the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' is Amy March from Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A general pardon granted by a state to offenders is the formal sense of this word.

clue.text: Rising sea surrounds old place filled with inhabitants

indicators.note: surrounds says the reversed sea word wraps round the others
Rising in a down entry means the word for sea is read upwards

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: A rising sea engulfs an old inhabited settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A land filled with residents has been populated, the adjectival past participle.

clue.text: Don't speak with favourites about dam replacement

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word for favourites round

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet
mum is the instruction to keep quiet, as in mum's the word

explanation.surface: Telling favoured people to keep quiet about replacing a water barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' looks like a reservoir wall but is a mother animal; a replacement mother is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is a mother, so a dam replacement is a stand-in mother acquired by remarriage.

clue.text: What makes tongue tingle and female diarist's heart flutter

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: heart takes the central letter of the word diarist

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet

explanation.surface: A sweet treat that excites a woman's diary-keeping heart.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small wager.
explanation.definitionFit: This fizzy powder sweet makes the tongue tingle when eaten.

clue.text: One fired up in purpose in revolution's territorial force

indicators.note: in places the one-and-fired-up pieces within the turned purpose word
in revolution means turned round, so the purpose word is read backwards

parts.note: aim means purpose
I is the Roman numeral one
lit means set alight, fired up

explanation.surface: A revolutionary militant fired up with purpose in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' turns the purpose word to MIA, and 'in' then places the other two pieces inside after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen army of part-time soldiers is a territorial force, as opposed to regular troops.

clue.text: Mass on Jovian moon topped landscape from millions of years ago

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons

indicators.note: topped means the first letter is cut off the landscape word

parts.note: a scene is a view or landscape

explanation.surface: A mass sits on a moon of Jupiter's ancient landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: This geological epoch ran from about 23 to 5 million years ago, so it is a prehistoric adjective.

clue.text: Target for darts having last of poison contained by drug's essence?

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the word poison

parts.note: in can mean contained by
E is ecstasy, the drug, so drug's gives E's
the core of something is its essence

explanation.surface: Poison darts imagined, aimed with a drug as its essence.
explanation.walkthrough: The darts target is 180, the maximum with three darts; nine score is 9 x 20, the same number.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine twenties make one hundred and eighty, the top score with three darts, so it is what a player aims for.

clue.text: Deal with opening position of queen's bishop's pawn in commentary?

indicators.note: in commentary means as spoken by a chess commentator

parts.words: opening position of queen's bishop's pawn
parts.note: White's queen's bishop's pawn starts on square c2

explanation.surface: Chess commentary on the opening square of a particular pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation the queen's bishop's pawn starts on c2, spoken 'see two'.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to or handle a task, as in 'I'll take care of it', is what dealing with means.

clue.text: Group from central Somalia with Farah, say, on location in Sweden

indicators.note: a group of letters from the central part of the word Somalia

parts.note: Mo Farah, the British distance runner, is an example of a Mo

explanation.surface: A Somali community joins Mo Farah at a spot in Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah is a Somali-born British Olympic champion at 5,000m and 10,000m.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a port city in southern Sweden, across the strait from Copenhagen.

clue.text: Sport is ultimately a disappointment for a philosopher

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: ultimately takes only the final letter of the word is

parts.note: a sell is a let-down or a disappointment

explanation.surface: A thinker finds sport a letdown in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A sell meaning a disappointment is British informal usage, as in 'what a sell'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell was the British logician and philosopher, so he is one example of the type.

clue.text: Black stone carried in anger, to show it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: carried in puts the stone abbreviation inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A black stone kept by someone furious, as a display of rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to anger, so the definition is 'to show anger'; anger also gives RILE in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: When hackles rise, a person visibly reacts with indignation, the verb's sense of displaying anger.

clue.text: Material providing strength and power for leading trio in film industry

indicators.note: for leading trio in means the first three letters are swapped out for the power letter

parts.note: Hollywood stands for the American film industry
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Strength and power are what the movie business needs at its top.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a board of glued wooden layers whose crossed grain gives it great strength.

clue.text: Lacking variations when contrarily stopping something they're based on?

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the inner piece sits inside

parts.note: musical variations are based on a theme

indicators.note: contrarily turns the word for when the other way round

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: An enigmatic remark about variations opposing what they build on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they' are the variations of the definition, so the thing they're based on is a theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any changes, everything identical, is how something unvaried stays.
